about: The neutral names cases use. A runner maps each to its own language; it adds no rule of its own.

key.note: The test key from the API description's signing test vector. Build the client with it.

client.base_url: the line the fake hub prints: http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1
client.waits: configure the client so a retry does not actually sleep (a Retry-After is honoured as a decision, not as wall time)

signing.sign.note: sign the message with the test key; no request is made

terminals.page.note: one page; count is the number of items in it

terminals.list.note: every terminal, following the cursor; ids in order. limit is the page size the SDK asks for, so a small one makes it follow the cursor

execution.place_order.note: never raises; exec_price is the fill price (a $decimal compares as a decimal), position is the position ticket (tickets.position), and a field the result does not carry is null

stream.read.note: open the stream against the fake hub (reconnecting allowed, no real wait between attempts), subscribe each channel in order, read until count data messages have arrived, then close. seqs and types are those messages in order; the rest are the stream's own counters: messages a seq gap proves were missed, connections after the first, 4009 and 4008 closes, resyncs, and channels the platform refused

stream.close_waiting.note: open the stream against the fake hub (reconnecting allowed, no real wait between attempts) and subscribe each channel in order. Start a read for the next message and leave it waiting while the hub sends nothing more (give it a moment, 100 ms). Close the stream. ended is true when the waiting read finished within 2 s with no message and no error; reconnects is the stream's count of connections after the first, which closing must leave at 0

markers.$decimal: an exact decimal, given as a string: pass the language's decimal type (Decimal, decimal, BigDecimal) or the string
markers.$float: a binary floating-point number: pass the language's float or double, to prove it is refused
markers.$fixture: already expanded by the fake hub before a runner sees the case

observe.returns: the call returned; each named field equals the value (a $decimal compares as a decimal)
observe.raises: the call raised (or rejected with) the named error kind; fields such as code and status equal the values
observe.refuses: the call refused before sending anything: invalid_argument is the language's argument or type error

live.about: Cases in live/ run against a real MFX Hub, not the fake one: no case scripts the hub's answer, so each holds a rule a real hub shows on its own. They run with the caller's own key, on a terminal that is logged in, and send at most one market order of the smallest volume, which the runner closes.

run.terminal_id: the run's terminal, logged in to a demo account
run.symbol: a symbol that server lists and quotes
run.md_channel: the ticks channel of symbol on server_id, as the SDK names it
run.min_volume: the symbol's smallest volume, as an exact decimal
run.unused_id: a new UUID no terminal has, made fresh for the case
run.new_key: a new idempotency key, made fresh for the case

case.client: test_key: build the client with the suite's test key instead of the caller's own. Absent: the caller's own key
case.needs: market: the case needs a market that is quoting. When the market does not answer in time the case is skipped, not failed

observe.returns: as for the fake hub; a {"$run": name} value is that run value
observe.includes: the call returned; each named list field includes the value
observe.exact: the call returned; each named field is exact: the language's decimal type or the decimal string the SDK keeps it as, never a binary float, and greater than zero
observe.ascending: the call returned; the named list rises strictly. Combined with returns, both hold
observe.repeat: make the call twice with the same arguments, idempotency key included. The second returns as repeat.returns says, and each field in repeat.same equals the first call's. Close any position either call opened
